title: Infrastructure Stability Model — Schema Repository Index
description: Machine-readable formalization of a thermodynamic infrastructure stability framework. Covers energy-material-labor network dynamics, latent node detection and activation, and intervention sequencing for 3-5 year critical window. Includes runnable simulation engines and a falsification ledger recording which claims have been tested and what the tests did to them.

theoretical_foundation.core_claim: Civilization-scale infrastructure systems can be modeled as coupled energy-material-labor networks. The binding constraint is not material scarcity but energy quality, skilled labor bandwidth, and maintenance-to-surplus ratio. Financial signals are a high-pass filter on physical system state — degradation is systematically invisible until nonlinear failure threshold is crossed.

key_variables.Phi: Maintenance burden ratio — primary stability metric. Phi = Em/(E*L_f). Bifurcation at Phi=1.0.
key_variables.L_f_active: Effective field labor bandwidth. Two channels: training (slow) and latent node recovery (fast).
key_variables.p_engage: Latent node activation probability. Sticky prior from institutional rejection. Updates on demonstrated evidence, not promises.
key_variables.R_i: Hazard recognition capacity. Propagates across trust network edges. Domain-portable.
key_variables.B_i: Signal obstruction. Must be reduced before activation outreach in the same locality, or hub nodes are burned.
key_variables.kappa: System coupling. Ratchet behavior. Amplifies cascade risk nonlinearly.
key_variables.epsilon: Labor exclusion coefficient from credential gating. Primary long-run control parameter.

key_insights.insight: Latent high-skill nodes exist in suppressed state. Recovery channel time constant is 0.5-2yr vs 3-7yr for training pipeline.
key_insights.note: Time constants are asserted from operational field knowledge, not measured.

key_insights.insight: Older high-R_i nodes are immediate stability amplifiers, not just labor units. Translational deployment to high-kappa interfaces multiplies their effect.

B_i reduction must precede activation outreach in the same locality. The cost of inverse order is topological, not aggregate: hub survival falls from 100% to 30% and inter-community connectivity to 44%, while total labor still improves over no intervention. The system is left connected enough to function and too fragmented to propagate again.
key_insights.superseded_wording: Inverse order creates re-suppression: confirmed dismissal drives p_engage to near-zero permanently. Most workforce initiatives fail here.

key_insights.insight: The sequencing constraint is local, not global. Regionally phased rollouts are safe — a region may begin activation while neighbours are still reducing B_i, provided each region's own B_i is down before its own outreach. Cross-boundary signal leakage does no measurable damage below ~4x its assumed intensity.
key_insights.conditional_on: leak_intensity in sim/network_sim.py, which is chosen rather than measured.

key_insights.insight: Activation via lateral trust network traversal outperforms institutional broadcast by order of magnitude. Signal fidelity is primary determinant, not outreach volume.
key_insights.note: Encoded as signal_fidelity and outreach_mode parameters in both simulation engines, but the order-of-magnitude ratio is assumed, not derived.

key_insights.insight: Marginal regime (0.7 < Phi < 1.0) is most dangerous because financial metrics do not detect it. Management signal lag tau is structural, not accidental.
Levers are coupled nonlinearly. Single-lever approaches fail above marginal regime. Order of operations is a constraint.
key_insights.note: Partially probed by the four-scenario ODE comparison, but no single-lever sweep has been run.

system_model.description: Core state variables, parameters, system constraints, intervention priority sequence.

node_detection_protocol.description: Step-by-step protocol for identifying, assessing, and activating latent high-skill nodes. Signal-based detection, lateral network traversal, B_i assessment, controlled deployment.
node_detection_protocol.primary_use: Field deployment by human coordinators or agent-based outreach systems

intervention_framework.description: State-to-action decision framework. Seven levers with time constants, impact ratings, prerequisites, and failure modes. Decision tree by system regime. Lever interaction matrix.
intervention_framework.primary_use: Decision support for coordinators, policy designers, or autonomous planning agents

measurement_protocol.description: Field-deployable physical metrics for Phi, L_f channels, p_engage, R_i, B_i, and kappa. Early warning dashboard. Short-tau physical reporting pipeline bypassing financial metric lag.
measurement_protocol.primary_use: Monitoring system design, dashboard construction, anomaly detection

falsification_protocol.description: The hypothesize-run-result-revise-search-rerun loop, the verdict vocabulary, and the rule that falsified artifacts move to legacy/ rather than being deleted or overwritten.
falsification_protocol.primary_use: Required reading before modifying any claim in this repository

falsification_ledger.description: Append-only record of every claim that has been tested, the exact test, the numbers, the verdict, the revised claim, and the unknowns the result opened.
falsification_ledger.primary_use: Determining what in this model is evidence and what is assertion

validator.description: Enforces the repository's own rules: JSON parses, no Unicode smart quotes, ledger entries carry every required field and a named unknown, ledger verdicts are in vocabulary, referenced artifacts and repository_map paths exist, and every audit module runs.
validator.primary_use: Run before committing any change to a schema or the ledger

ode_engine.description: Mean-field ODE integration of the 5-variable coupled system. Four intervention scenarios, parameter sensitivity sweeps, temporal cohort handoff, stochastic shock Monte Carlo.

agent_based_engine.description: Agent-based simulation over a Watts-Strogatz trust network with heterogeneous R_i. Captures what the mean-field model cannot: hub burn, community fragmentation, bridge-node loss, and partial-order regional phasing.

audit_modules.description: Independent, stdlib-only diagnostic modules. Each runs standalone and prints its own report. Not unified behind a shared bus — see ledger F-005.
audit_modules.note: Several are prose specifications in Python form rather than computation. Verdict for those is 'untested'; they are not evidence.

figures.description: Generated output. Reproducible by rerunning the simulation engines; overwritten rather than archived.
figures.regenerate: python3 sim/sim.py all && python3 sim/network_sim.py all

legacy.description: Falsified, superseded, and orphaned artifacts. Retained as evidence, paired with ledger entries. Not maintained, not imported by live code, not deleted.

extension_roadmap.item: simulation_engine: Python or Julia ODE system from schema parameters
agent_based_activation_model: p_engage update dynamics in heterogeneous population
cohort_temporal_handoff_model: older node retirement curve vs younger node ramp
network_graph_tooling: trust network construction from field sociometric data
extension_roadmap.gap: Networks are synthetic (Watts-Strogatz, planted communities). No field sociometric data has been ingested. Ledger F-003 names this as the highest-value open unknown.

extension_roadmap.item: geographic_node_distribution: latent pool sizing by region and trade
extension_roadmap.gap: Communities are synthetic and equally sized. No regional or trade-specific pool sizing.

extension_roadmap.item: real_us_labor_data_integration: BLS vacancy rates, apprenticeship enrollment
second_campaign_simulation: intervention run through a hub-depleted network
extension_roadmap.rationale: Ledger F-003 locates the cost of wrong-order activation in the difficulty of the next campaign. That cost has never been simulated.
Ledger F-004's partial-order safety result is conditional on this parameter.

how_to_use.for_human_coordinators: Start with node-detection.json. Run steps 1-4 before any outreach. Then decision-framework.json for lever sequencing. Check legacy/ledger.json for which of the claims you are relying on have actually been tested.
how_to_use.for_ai_agents: Parse system-model.json for state variable definitions and parameter schemas. Use the decision_tree in decision-framework.json for state-to-action mapping. Use measurement.json for metric definitions and early warning thresholds. Read legacy/ledger.json before treating any key_insight as established — evidence_status fields distinguish confirmed from asserted.
how_to_use.for_researchers: system-model.json contains the full ODE structure; sim/sim.py implements it. The open unknowns most worth attacking are listed in legacy/ledger.json under open_unknowns_summary.
how_to_use.for_policy_designers: decision-framework.json lever_interaction_matrix and decision_tree. measurement.json early_warning_dashboard for monitoring requirements. Note that the sequencing constraint has been narrowed — see ledger F-002 through F-004 before designing around it.

provenance.development_method: Collaborative formalization from working conversation. Grounded in thermodynamic infrastructure analysis, complex systems theory (Tainter, West), and operational field knowledge of rural industrial labor systems.
provenance.validation_status: Structurally simulated, empirically unparameterized. The ODE and agent-based models run and their results are recorded in legacy/ledger.json. No parameter in either model has been calibrated against field data. Two model claims have been falsified and revised by their own simulations; one has been confirmed against a strengthened test.
provenance.note: This model was developed and distributed using its own principles: lateral network delivery, open access, no institutional gatekeeping.
